title: Certify P112 block-rank lower bound nine and exact binary broadcast rate
body:
This package closes below-nine compression of the pinned P112 fitting graph across all block sizes. Every fitting matrix with invertible d-by-d diagonal blocks has rank at least 9d over every field; the inherited binary construction attains 9d in characteristic two. Even nonlinear zero-error codes for d-bit messages require exactly 9d broadcast bits.

The source-pinned witness has 14 vertices and is four isolated vertices plus Petersen in the usual fitting/side-information convention. A separate four-clique argument proves the characteristic-two result directly. An exact 113-term rational certificate replays the known Petersen lower bound five, then a documented row-space/entropy reduction gives the stronger claims. Petersen's rate is credited to Blasiak–Kleinberg–Lubetzky, Fact 5.6(1); the binary E8/symplectic upper construction is credited to Leung et al. and Peeters. No novelty claim is made for those known results.

Validation: the registered Python 3.12 package passes with both verifiers under -I -B -O and no third-party dependencies. It checks all 2,912 required-zero pairs, all 12,544 binary Gram entries, the exact induced-graph isomorphism, all 1,024 rational coefficient sums, a matching positive fixture, and 15 meaningful corruption controls. Metadata/source pins and git diff --check pass. Independent AI proof review checked the all-field and nonlinear reductions. These are finite certificates plus written proofs, not proof-assistant formalization.

This is a side result of the helper-inventory investigation: no native word, paid supplier improvement, selected-frontier change, or multiplication-exponent gain is claimed. The useful next question must change the graph/interface constraints or save other paid work. Base/source commit: 0b1cccf86e2f5132ed286a26ef0a681a495740ea. Scope, source hashes, replay commands, limitations, inherited input attribution and open questions are in the package. Coordination: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1713.

Prepared for Thiago with substantial OpenAI GPT-6 Astra and Codex assistance. Apache-2.0; predecessor attribution retained.
